title: Oversized peer RSA keys allow excessive CPU consumption during DTLS handshakes
summary: Peer RSA public keys were not size-limited before signature verification. A remote peer can supply a certificate with an attacker-chosen oversized modulus and invalid signature; expensive verification occurs before rejection. Repeated or concurrent handshakes can consume CPU and delay legitimate connections. The fix rejects RSA keys above 8,192 bits.
ai_role: The Pion maintainer's case-specific advisory credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier 3X1BUF5Y). It does not identify model versions or internal discovery dates.
classification_note: The cited advisory documents public disclosure; it does not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: The advisory identifies fix commit fa6e8d3 and the following package-version scope: v2 2.0.0–2.2.12 (no patched v2 version listed); v3 3.0.0 through before 3.1.13, fixed 3.1.13. This source does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: CPU consumption and reduced availability under repeated or concurrent malicious handshakes; affected WebRTC applications only when the attacker reaches an RSA verification path.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible attack path but does not report observed exploitation.
